stemMd: An object is 30 cm from a thin converging lens of focal length 10 cm. What is the image distance in the thin-lens model?
explanationMd: Use 1/f = 1/u + 1/v. Then 1/v = 1/10 − 1/30 = 2/30 = 1/15, giving v = 15 cm. The positive image distance corresponds to a real image on the opposite side of the lens.

distractorRationale.d: This subtracts focal length from object distance rather than using reciprocal distances.
distractorRationale.e: Equal object and image distances would occur at twice the focal length.
distractorRationale.b: This incorrectly adds the object reciprocal to the focal reciprocal for the image.
distractorRationale.c: The object is beyond the focal point, so the image is real on the opposite side.
